BUS-4KV-B source breakers CB-203/CB-202/CB-303 are not made mutually adjacent through the bus; each connects to BUS-4KV-B.
BUS-480-C is not connected directly to MCC-2A in the matrix; the modeled path is through CB-M2A despite a visually close dogleg/riser.
BUS-480-D is not connected directly to MCC-2B in the matrix; the modeled path is through CB-M2B despite a visually close dogleg/riser.
MCC-1A and MCC-2A are not connected to each other; nearby vertical conductors are feeder/dogleg routes, not an MCC tie.
MCC-1B and MCC-2B are not connected to each other; nearby vertical conductors and load drops are not a bus tie.
DC-BUS-A and DC-BUS-B are not directly tied; each feeds its own inverter, and ATS-INV handles the downstream AC transfer path.
DC-BUS-A is not connected directly to ATS-INV; the path goes through INV-1A.
DC-BUS-B is not connected directly to ATS-INV; the path goes through INV-1B.
PNL-ESFAS-A and PNL-ESFAS-B are not directly connected to each other; both are separately associated with BUS-120VAC-ESF/SEQ-REC-1.
Terminal-block fan-out pins are not expanded into anonymous junction nodes.
label_ambiguities: The load labels use both PUMP and PMP abbreviations; PMP-BOR-A/B and PMP-LUBE-A/B are kept as printed-looking abbreviations.
PUMP-RHR A1 and PUMP-RHR B1 are normalized as PUMP-RHR-A1 and PUMP-RHR-B1.
The upper labels TB-A/TB-B appear to describe terminal-block groups; the matrix node uses the more specific printed block labels TB-RPS-A and TB-RPS-B.
CB-DC-1A/B source side is modeled from MCC-2A/MCC-2B because the visible risers continue from those MCC buses into the charger breaker area.
PT-4160A/B bus taps are asserted, while their long dotted protective-signal routes are kept uncertain.
